svg.title: Optional CAN Loopback Wiring: Monitoring Alongside an Active Original TCU
svg.text: Optional Adapter Variation: Looping CAN Buses Back to Original TCU (Passive Monitoring Mode)
Routes IT-CAN (3->11, 4->12) and/or M-CAN / AV-CAN (5->13, 6->14) back to the factory TCU so the original TCU stays connected.
1. DEVICE SIDE (16-Pin Male — Add Loopback Jumpers)
2. CAR SIDE (16-Pin Female -> Returns to 40-Pin TCU)
Top row (1–6) loops to Bottom row (9–14)
Dashed loops (11–14): populate for whichever bus(es) should also reach Original TCU
Pins 1–6: Unpinned OEM | Pins 9–14: Return to TCU
Important — Avoid Active CAN Transmit Collisions When Looping CAN Back to the Original TCU:
• If IT-CAN (#6/#7 via Pins 11–12) is looped back to an active original TCU, use simppeliTCU for PASSIVE MONITORING ONLY (do not trigger climate, charge,
or lock commands, as both TCUs transmitting 0x56E frames will collide). You can also loop one bus while isolating the other simply by adding/removing jumpers!
